claims.text: Applying quantum Monte Carlo techniques to the target magnetic system will reveal a ferromagnetic ground state.
QMC can accurately resolve subtle free-energy differences between competing magnetic orders.
A transition-metal-based high-entropy alloy can have a paramagnetic initial state with fluctuating local moments.
The candidate system is modeled by DFT in a disordered-local-moment paramagnetic state.
Electron-electron correlations play an important role in the candidate system.
QMC provides comprehensive sampling of low-energy magnetic configurations.
The relevant calculation should be performed in the low-temperature, T approaching zero, regime.
Simulation parameters can be chosen to capture strong electron correlations and exchange interactions.
Free-energy calculations can describe magnetic and structural states while accounting for magnetic fluctuations.
Subtle free-energy differences between ferromagnetic and alternative magnetic orders can be resolved near the ground state.
QMC accurately treats electron-electron interactions and exchange correlations.
Full QMC sampling of low-energy configurations allows an energetic preference for ferromagnetism to emerge.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have a statistically lower free energy than competing magnetic orders.
A statistically lower free energy for the ferromagnetic configuration indicates a ferromagnetic ground state.
Conventional DFT initiated from a disordered-local-moment state may underestimate electron-correlation effects.
Conventional DFT may fail to resolve small energy differences between magnetic configurations.
The calculated free-energy difference and robustness of ferromagnetism may depend on finite-size effects, trial-wavefunction quality, and other QMC parameters.
Improved sampling is expected to qualitatively predict a ferromagnetic ground state.
Quantitative energy differences remain uncertain and require computational and experimental validation.
Failure to find a statistically significant and parameter-robust free-energy advantage for ferromagnetism would falsify the hypothesis.
